sentence: Solid-phase peptide synthesis anchors the growing chain to an insoluble resin so that excess reagents and byproducts are washed away after each coupling. The chain is extended from the carboxyl terminus toward the amino terminus through repeated cycles of deprotection and coupling, and the finished peptide is cleaved from the resin with strong acid at the end.

A solubility curve coupled to acid-base chemistry governs the dissolution of metal hydroxides. Aluminium hydroxide is amphoteric, dissolving in acid as the hexaaquo cation and in strong base as the tetrahydroxoaluminate anion. Its minimum solubility lies near pH 6 to 7, which is exploited in water treatment where flocculation of aluminium hydroxide sweeps suspended particulates from the supply.

High-temperature superconductivity in YBa2Cu3O7-delta arises in copper oxide planes where holes doped from charge-reservoir layers pair below a critical temperature of 92 kelvin. The d-wave order parameter has nodes along the Brillouin zone diagonals, distinguishing the pairing symmetry from conventional s-wave BCS superconductors. Oxygen stoichiometry delta near 0.07 optimises Tc, and chain ordering of the labile O(1) sites strongly influences carrier density.

Allylic carbocations are stabilised by resonance that delocalises the positive charge over two terminal carbons. A nucleophile may then attack either terminus, giving products of direct and of allylic-shifted substitution. The ratio of the two depends on the relative stability and steric accessibility of the two possible attack sites within the delocalised cation.

Fischer esterification couples a carboxylic acid and an alcohol under acid catalysis to give an ester and water. Every step is reversible, so the equilibrium is driven toward ester by using an excess of one reactant or by removing water. Isotopic labelling shows that the ester oxygen originates from the alcohol, not the acid.

The Boltzmann distribution gives the probability of a system in state i with energy E_i as proportional to exp(-E_i/kT), where k is the Boltzmann constant and T the absolute temperature. The partition function Q = sum exp(-E_i/kT) normalises the distribution and links microscopic energy levels to macroscopic thermodynamic quantities through Helmholtz free energy A = -kT ln Q.

A chain reaction proceeds through initiation, propagation, and termination steps, and may show explosive behaviour when branching steps generate more radicals than they consume. The hydrogen-oxygen reaction exhibits three explosion limits in a pressure-temperature diagram, the lower and upper limits set by competition between wall recombination, gas-phase branching, and three-body chain-terminating collisions.

Fluorine-19 nuclear magnetic resonance is highly sensitive because the isotope is the only naturally occurring one and has a spin of one half. The enormous range of fluorine chemical shifts, spanning several hundred parts per million, makes the technique exquisitely responsive to small changes in chemical environment and a powerful probe of binding and conformation in fluorinated molecules.

Cerium in the plus four state is a clean one-electron oxidant widely used in titrimetry because its reduction to the plus three state involves no change in coordination geometry and no oxygen transfer. The sharp potential near 1.44 volts in sulphuric acid and the stability of the reagent make ceric titrations a precise alternative to permanganate for determining iron and oxalate.

Expanded octets appear in third-row and heavier elements, which can accommodate more than eight valence electrons. Sulphur in sulphur hexafluoride is surrounded by six bonding pairs in an octahedral arrangement. Modern bonding descriptions favour three-centre four-electron interactions over genuine d-orbital participation to account for the hypervalent geometry.

Hess's law states that the enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the path taken, because enthalpy is a state function. The enthalpy of a target reaction can therefore be assembled by adding the enthalpies of a sequence of known reactions that sum to it, reversing any reaction's sign when its direction is flipped.

Beta-minus decay converts a neutron into a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino, so the atomic number rises by one while the mass number is unchanged. Carbon-14 decays this way to nitrogen-14. Because the emitted energy is shared with the unseen antineutrino, beta particles emerge with a continuous spectrum of energies up to a sharp endpoint.

Photosynthetic electron transport in chloroplast thylakoids couples water oxidation at photosystem II to NADP+ reduction at photosystem I, generating ATP through a proton motive force across the thylakoid membrane. The oxygen-evolving complex extracts four electrons from two water molecules in a stepwise S-state cycle catalysed by a Mn4CaO5 cluster.

Alkylation of the acetoacetic ester enolate followed by acid hydrolysis and decarboxylation provides a general synthesis of substituted methyl ketones. The active methylene flanked by two carbonyls is acidic enough for mild bases, and once the carbon skeleton is built the beta-keto acid loses carbon dioxide on heating through a cyclic six-membered transition state.

Fragment-based drug discovery starts from low-molecular-weight chemical fragments of 150 to 300 daltons that bind weakly at micromolar to millimolar affinity. Crystallography or NMR identifies the binding pose, and iterative growing or linking elaborates the fragment toward nanomolar affinity. Venetoclax, a BCL-2 inhibitor for chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, emerged from this strategy applied to the hydrophobic groove that normally accommodates BH3-only proteins.

Boron in BF3 is sp2 hybridised with an empty p orbital perpendicular to the molecular plane, making it a strong Lewis acid. Adduct formation with an electron pair donor such as NH3 produces tetrahedral H3N-BF3, with reorganisation of B from sp2 to sp3 and quenching of the empty p orbital by donation of the nitrogen lone pair into the new sigma bond.

Targeted protein degradation through PROTACs joins a target-binding ligand and an E3 ligase-recruiting moiety through a flexible linker. The resulting bifunctional molecule induces ternary complex formation between target, ligase, and PROTAC, leading to ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of the target. Catalytic mechanism of action and event-driven rather than occupancy-driven pharmacology give degraders advantages over conventional inhibitors of so-called undruggable scaffolding proteins.

Deprotonation of a ketone at the alpha carbon by a strong, non-nucleophilic base such as lithium diisopropylamide generates an enolate whose negative charge is delocalised onto oxygen. Performing the deprotonation cold under kinetic control favours the less substituted enolate, because the base abstracts the more accessible proton faster than it can reach equilibrium.

Silane reacts with water only when catalysed by trace base, unlike the inert methane, because silicon can expand its coordination sphere and accept nucleophilic attack at the central atom. The hydrolysis liberates hydrogen and forms silica gel, and the susceptibility of the silicon-hydrogen bond underlies the use of silanes as reducing agents.

Body-centred cubic iron places one atom at each corner of the unit cell and one at the body centre, giving two atoms per cell and a packing efficiency of 68 percent. The atoms touch along the body diagonal, so the diagonal length of root three times the lattice parameter equals four atomic radii, allowing the radius to be calculated directly from the measured cell edge.

The Wittig reaction converts an aldehyde or ketone to an alkene by treatment with a phosphonium ylide. The ylide adds to the carbonyl to give a betaine that cyclises to an oxaphosphetane, which fragments to the alkene and triphenylphosphine oxide. Stabilised ylides produce predominantly the E-alkene, while unstabilised ylides under salt-free conditions favour the Z-alkene.

Capillary rise in a thin tube of radius r occurs to height h = 2 gamma cos theta / (rho g r) when the liquid wets the tube. The equation derives from balancing surface tension against the gravitational weight of the supported column. For water in a clean glass capillary of 0.1 millimetre radius, h reaches roughly 15 centimetres, a phenomenon central to soil water movement and chromatographic separations on paper.

A chiral auxiliary is a removable enantiopure group attached to a substrate to bias the stereochemistry of a subsequent reaction. The Evans oxazolidinone directs alkylation and aldol reactions of the attached acyl group with high diastereoselectivity, and after the new stereocentre is set the auxiliary is cleaved and recovered for reuse.

subtopic: peptide bond formation and protecting groups
sentence: The fluorenylmethyloxycarbonyl group protects the amino terminus during peptide synthesis and is removed under mild basic conditions with piperidine, which abstracts a fluorenyl proton and triggers an elimination releasing carbon dioxide and dibenzofulvene. Its base-lability makes it orthogonal to the acid-labile side-chain protecting groups used alongside it.

Asymmetric hydrogenation with a rhodium complex bearing a chiral bisphosphine ligand reduces a prochiral enamide to a single enantiomer of an amino acid derivative. The chiral pocket discriminates between the two faces of the bound alkene, and the major enantiomer often arises from the less stable diastereomeric catalyst-substrate complex because it reacts faster.

A nitrile is hydrolysed to a carboxylic acid under either acidic or basic aqueous conditions, passing through an amide intermediate. The transformation extends a carbon chain by one carbon when the nitrile is first installed by displacing a halide with cyanide, providing a classic two-step route from an alkyl halide to the homologous carboxylic acid.

The thermal ring opening of cyclobutene to butadiene is an electrocyclic reaction of a four-electron system and therefore proceeds conrotatory. When the cyclobutene bears two methyl groups, the conrotatory motion dictates which geometric isomer of the diene forms; the cis dimethyl compound opens exclusively to one stereoisomer, a clean experimental test of the orbital-symmetry prediction.

The molar solubility of a salt with formula AB2 is not simply the square root of its solubility product. If the solid dissolves to give s moles of A and 2s moles of B, the ion product is s times (2s) squared, equal to four s cubed, so the solubility is the cube root of one quarter of the solubility product.

Forster resonance energy transfer between a donor and acceptor chromophore varies as the inverse sixth power of separation, F = 1 / (1 + (r/R_0)^6), making it a molecular ruler over distances 1 to 10 nanometres. The Forster radius R_0 depends on donor emission and acceptor absorption spectral overlap, refractive index, and orientation factor. Single-pair FRET experiments at the molecular level reveal conformational dynamics of biomolecules.

Autoxidation of an organic substrate by atmospheric oxygen is a radical chain in which a carbon radical adds oxygen to form a peroxyl radical, which abstracts a hydrogen to give a hydroperoxide and a new carbon radical. The accumulation of hydroperoxides explains the gradual rancidification of fats and the formation of explosive peroxides in aged ethers.

Pyridine is aromatic because its nitrogen contributes one electron to the pi sextet while its lone pair occupies an sp2 orbital in the ring plane, free for protonation and metal coordination. Pyrrole is also aromatic, but its nitrogen donates both lone-pair electrons into the pi system, leaving the molecule a weak base and a reactive substrate toward electrophiles.

Polar aprotic solvents such as dimethyl sulfoxide and dimethylformamide accelerate SN2 reactions dramatically. They solvate cations strongly through their negative dipole ends but cannot hydrogen-bond to anions, leaving the nucleophile poorly solvated and therefore far more reactive than the same anion in water or an alcohol.

Cyclodextrins are cyclic oligosaccharides of glucose units that form a truncated-cone cavity hydrophobic enough to host nonpolar guests in water. Beta-cyclodextrin with seven glucose units encapsulates small aromatic molecules with binding constants typically 10^2 to 10^5 inverse molar. Industrial applications include taste masking of bitter pharmaceuticals, solubilisation of hydrophobic dyes, and stabilisation of volatile fragrances in detergents.

Migratory insertion of carbon monoxide into a metal-alkyl bond proceeds through coordination of CO at a vacant site on the metal followed by migration of the alkyl group from metal to coordinated carbonyl. The resulting metal-acyl species is the key intermediate in the cobalt-catalysed hydroformylation and the Monsanto rhodium-catalysed acetic acid synthesis from methanol and CO.

An epoxide is opened by nucleophiles under both acidic and basic conditions, but with opposite regioselectivity. Under basic conditions the nucleophile attacks the less hindered carbon in an SN2 fashion, whereas under acidic conditions the protonated epoxide develops carbocation character at the more substituted carbon, directing the nucleophile there instead.

Gaussian basis sets approximate atomic orbitals as contracted linear combinations of primitive Gaussian functions, sacrificing the cusp at the nucleus for efficient evaluation of multi-centre two-electron integrals. The Pople sets 6-31G(d,p) and Dunning correlation-consistent cc-pVTZ provide standardised starting points; basis set superposition error is corrected with the counterpoise procedure when computing intermolecular interactions.

Real gases deviate from ideality at high pressure and low temperature, and the van der Waals equation corrects for this with two terms. The a constant accounts for attractive intermolecular forces that reduce the measured pressure, and the b constant subtracts the finite volume occupied by the molecules themselves, giving (P plus a n squared over V squared) times (V minus n b) equal to nRT.

Zeolites are crystalline aluminosilicates with regularly spaced channels and cavities of molecular dimensions. ZSM-5, a pentasil framework with intersecting 10-membered ring channels of 0.55 nanometre diameter, serves as the workhorse catalyst for the methanol-to-gasoline process and fluid catalytic cracking. Isomorphous substitution of aluminium for silicon introduces Bronsted acid sites whose strength and number govern catalytic activity and selectivity.

Tropospheric ozone forms by photolysis of nitrogen dioxide at wavelengths below 420 nanometres, producing atomic oxygen that combines with O2 in the presence of a third body to give O3. Volatile organic compounds accelerate the cycle by converting NO to NO2 without consuming ozone, leading to the elevated ozone levels of urban photochemical smog episodes during sunny summer afternoons.

Chromium speciation determines toxicity in industrial effluents: Cr(III) is a poorly absorbed essential trace nutrient while Cr(VI) is a powerful oxidiser and known human carcinogen. Treatment of chromate-bearing wastewater proceeds by reduction with sodium sulphite or ferrous sulphate at low pH, followed by precipitation of Cr(OH)3 at pH 8 to 9. The amphoteric hydroxide redissolves above pH 11, narrowing the precipitation window.

A sigmatropic hydrogen shift relocates a hydrogen atom along a pi system together with the sigma bond that holds it. A thermal [1,5] hydrogen shift in a cyclopentadiene is suprafacial and symmetry allowed, the hydrogen moving across the same face of the ring, whereas a thermal [1,3] shift would require an antarafacial geometry that is too strained to occur readily.

Hydride shifts allow a carbocation to relocate along a carbon chain, and a cascade of successive 1,2-hydride shifts can move positive charge several carbons from its origin. Each shift is favoured only if it produces a cation of equal or greater stability, so the charge migrates toward more substituted positions and toward sites stabilised by adjacent heteroatoms.

The carbonic acid bicarbonate system buffers blood near pH 7.4. Dissolved carbon dioxide hydrates to carbonic acid, which dissociates to bicarbonate and a proton with an effective pKa of 6.1. The lungs adjust the carbon dioxide partial pressure and the kidneys adjust bicarbonate, so the open buffer operates far more effectively than a closed system fixed at its pKa would predict.

Surfactant micelles form above the critical micelle concentration when amphiphilic molecules aggregate to shield hydrophobic tails from water. Sodium dodecyl sulphate in water has a CMC near 8 millimolar and an aggregation number around 62, giving spherical micelles roughly 4 nanometres in diameter. Above 1 weight percent the geometry transitions through rods, hexagonal cylinders, and lamellae as packing parameter v/(a_0 l_c) increases.

The zinc blende structure of cubic zinc sulphide has sulphide ions in a face-centred cubic array with zinc ions occupying half the tetrahedral holes in an ordered alternating pattern. Each ion is four-coordinate, and the structure is adopted by many semiconductors including gallium arsenide, whose direct band gap underpins its use in light-emitting diodes and high-frequency electronics.

Heterogeneous ammonia synthesis on iron-based catalysts proceeds through dissociative chemisorption of N2 on the Fe(111) surface as the rate-determining step, with activation energy near 75 kilojoules per mole. Subsequent hydrogenation of surface N atoms via NH and NH2 intermediates leads to NH3 desorption. Potassium promotion lowers the binding energy of N* by donating electrons into the metal, accelerating the rate-limiting step.

Cucurbiturils are barrel-shaped molecules formed by condensation of glycoluril with formaldehyde, with carbonyl-rimmed portals and hydrophobic cavities. CB[7] hosts adamantylammonium guests with binding constants reaching 10^15 inverse molar in water, exceeding the avidin-biotin interaction. The unusually strong affinity arises from the high desolvation energy of the hydrophobic cavity coupled with ion-dipole interactions at the rims.

Van der Waals radii define the effective size of an atom in non-bonded contact, the distance of closest approach before repulsion dominates. The van der Waals radius of hydrogen is about 120 picometres, and steric strain in crowded molecules arises when atoms are forced closer than the sum of their van der Waals radii, raising the energy through repulsive overlap.

The Corey-Bakshi-Shibata reduction uses a chiral oxazaborolidine catalyst to reduce a prochiral ketone to a secondary alcohol of defined configuration. Borane coordinates to the catalyst nitrogen while the ketone binds to boron, and the rigid six-membered transition state transfers hydride to one face selectively, giving enantiomeric excesses commonly exceeding 95 percent.

The retro-Diels-Alder reaction fragments a cyclohexene into a diene and a dienophile when entropy and the release of a stable small molecule favour it. Cyclopentadiene stored as its dimer cracks on heating, the dimer undergoing retro-Diels-Alder to regenerate two molecules of monomer that are collected by distillation before they redimerise.

The carbon dioxide molecule is linear and non-polar despite containing two polar carbon-oxygen bonds, because the bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel. Water, by contrast, is bent, so its two oxygen-hydrogen bond dipoles add to a net dipole moment, the geometric difference accounting for the contrasting physical properties of the two simple oxides.

The mevalonate pathway supplies isopentenyl pyrophosphate in animals and fungi, beginning with condensation of three acetyl-CoA units into hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA. Reduction to mevalonate, two phosphorylations, and a decarboxylative elimination then deliver the activated five-carbon building block from which all isoprenoids in those organisms ultimately descend.

Covalent kinase inhibitors target a non-catalytic cysteine residue near the ATP-binding site through a Michael acceptor warhead such as an acrylamide. Ibrutinib forms an irreversible bond to Cys481 of Bruton's tyrosine kinase, prolonging the duration of target inhibition beyond the plasma half-life. Selectivity arises because most other kinases lack a cysteine at the analogous position; the few that share it constitute the off-target profile.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy probes electrode interfaces by applying a small sinusoidal voltage and measuring the complex impedance over a wide frequency range. The Randles circuit, comprising solution resistance in series with a parallel combination of double-layer capacitance and charge-transfer resistance with Warburg diffusion impedance, fits most simple electron-transfer reactions and yields kinetic and mass-transport parameters from Nyquist plots.

Calorimetry at constant pressure, as in a simple coffee-cup apparatus, measures heat directly as the enthalpy change of the reaction. The heat absorbed or released equals the mass of solution times its specific heat times the temperature change, and dividing by the moles of limiting reagent gives the molar enthalpy of the process.

Nighttime atmospheric chemistry is dominated by the nitrate radical NO3, formed by reaction of NO2 with ozone. NO3 in equilibrium with N2O5 oxidises emitted alkenes and reacts with deliquesced aerosol surfaces to release ClNO2, a daytime chlorine atom source that contributes to ozone formation. The chemistry quenches at dawn as photolysis of NO3 destroys it on a timescale of seconds.

Singlet oxygen produced by photosensitisation with a triplet-state photosensitiser such as rose bengal undergoes [4+2] cycloaddition with conjugated dienes to give endoperoxides. With allylic systems the ene reaction predominates, transferring a hydrogen and bonding the oxygen to give an allyl hydroperoxide. These transformations are exploited in synthesis of natural-product hydroperoxides and in selective oxygenations under mild conditions.

A carboxylic acid is converted to an acyl chloride by reagents such as thionyl chloride or oxalyl chloride, which first transform the hydroxyl into a far better leaving group. Chloride then displaces it through the addition-elimination sequence, and the byproducts, sulfur dioxide or carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide, escape as gases that drive the reaction to completion.

Electroplating copper from acidic copper sulphate baths with leveller and brightener additives produces smooth bright deposits suitable for printed circuit fabrication. The additives, typically polyethylene glycol, chloride ion, and sulphopropyl disulphide, adsorb selectively at high-current-density features and suppress deposition there, redirecting current to recessed regions and filling vias from the bottom up without seams.

The Paal-Knorr synthesis builds five-membered heterocycles from 1,4-dicarbonyl compounds. Treatment with a primary amine yields a pyrrole, with phosphorus pentasulfide a thiophene, and with acid a furan, in each case through cyclisation and loss of water. The reaction is a reliable route to substituted azoles when the dicarbonyl precursor is accessible.

Molecular dynamics simulations propagate atomic positions through Newton's equations using a force field that parameterises bonded interactions as harmonic springs and torsion terms plus non-bonded Lennard-Jones and Coulombic pieces. The velocity Verlet integrator with a femtosecond time step conserves energy in a microcanonical ensemble. Thermostats such as Nose-Hoover and barostats such as Parrinello-Rahman impose temperature and pressure control while sampling the canonical and NPT ensembles respectively.

The Heck reaction couples an aryl halide and an alkene under palladium catalysis to give a styrene-type product without retaining a metal-bound intermediate. Oxidative addition of Ar-X to Pd(0), alkene coordination and migratory insertion, beta-hydride elimination, and base-mediated regeneration of Pd(0) close the cycle. The vinyl product retains the trans geometry preferred in the beta-hydride elimination step.

The radius ratio rule predicts coordination geometry in ionic solids from the ratio of cation to anion radius. A ratio between 0.414 and 0.732 favours octahedral six-coordination as in sodium chloride, while a ratio above 0.732 permits eight-coordination as in caesium chloride. The rule reflects the geometric requirement that anions not overlap while the cation contacts each of its neighbours.

The reaction field of a polar solvent stabilises a polar transition state in proportion to the change in dipole moment along the reaction coordinate. A reaction in which charge is created or separated speeds up in a more polar solvent, while a reaction in which charge is destroyed or dispersed slows down, a pattern captured by Hughes-Ingold solvent rules.

Dynamic covalent chemistry exploits reversible bond formation under thermodynamic control to assemble complex architectures from simpler components. Imine formation between aldehydes and amines, disulphide exchange between thiols, and boronate ester formation between diols and boronic acids each provide a reversible linkage. Combinatorial libraries generated by mixing multiple components self-edit under selection pressure from a target, producing the highest-affinity binder enriched in the equilibrium mixture.

Photoredox catalysis with ruthenium tris-bipyridyl complexes harnesses visible light to access single-electron transfer chemistry. Excitation generates a long-lived metal-to-ligand charge-transfer triplet state, which oxidises or reduces a substrate at potentials of plus or minus 0.8 volts versus SCE. The resulting radical intermediates couple, add to alkenes, or abstract hydrogen, enabling cross-couplings, decarboxylative reactions, and C-H functionalisations under mild conditions.

The aromatic stabilisation of benzene is quantified by comparing its experimental heat of hydrogenation with three times that of cyclohexene. The measured value falls short of the prediction by roughly 150 kilojoules per mole, and this resonance energy reflects the extra stability conferred by delocalising the six pi electrons over all six carbon atoms.

Crystal field theory accounts for the colour and magnetism of transition metal complexes by considering the electrostatic splitting of d orbitals by the surrounding ligand field. In an octahedral field the d orbitals split into a lower t2g triplet and an upper eg doublet, separated by the crystal field splitting parameter 10Dq, whose magnitude determines whether the complex is high or low spin.

Calixarenes are bowl-shaped phenolic cyclic oligomers obtained by base-catalysed condensation of para-substituted phenols with formaldehyde. The cone conformation of calix[4]arene presents four hydroxyls at the lower rim and four para substituents at the upper rim, providing orthogonal handles for functionalisation. Tetraester derivatives selectively extract sodium ion over potassium with ratios above 1000, exploiting the size-match of the cation to the carbonyl-rimmed cavity.

The carbon-fluorine bond is the strongest single bond carbon forms, with a dissociation energy near 480 kilojoules per mole, owing to the small size of fluorine and the strong electrostatic component of the highly polar bond. This strength confers exceptional thermal and chemical stability on perfluorinated compounds and underlies the inertness of fully fluorinated materials.

Glutamate provides the umami taste through its binding to the T1R1/T1R3 receptor on the tongue. The naturally occurring L-glutamate in tomatoes, parmesan, soy sauce, and mushrooms triggers the same receptor as monosodium glutamate added as a seasoning. Synergy with the ribonucleotides inosinate and guanylate produces an eightfold amplification of perceived intensity, accounting for the depth of flavour in stocks combining meat with mushrooms or seaweed.

Galvanic protection of steel pipelines uses sacrificial zinc or magnesium anodes that corrode preferentially because their reduction potentials are more negative than iron. Connecting the anode to the structure through a wire establishes the protection circuit; corrosion currents flow off the buried anode rather than the steel. Impressed-current systems substitute a power supply for the sacrificial metal, allowing inert mixed-metal-oxide anodes to deliver controlled cathodic polarisation.

Polymorphism allows a single compound to crystallise in distinct lattice arrangements with different physical properties. Calcium carbonate occurs as rhombohedral calcite and orthorhombic aragonite, the former thermodynamically stable at ambient conditions. In pharmaceuticals the choice of polymorph controls dissolution rate and bioavailability, making polymorph screening a regulated step in drug development.

The Diels-Alder reaction is a thermal [4+2] cycloaddition between a conjugated diene in the s-cis conformation and a dienophile bearing electron-withdrawing groups. The concerted suprafacial-suprafacial transition state preserves the stereochemistry of both partners, giving the endo adduct preferentially due to secondary orbital interactions in the transition state.

Ultraviolet-visible absorption spectroscopy measures electronic transitions, principally pi to pi-star and n to pi-star transitions in conjugated organic chromophores. The Beer-Lambert law A = epsilon c l relates absorbance to molar absorptivity, concentration, and path length, providing the basis for quantitative analysis of solutions when extinction coefficients are known.

Coupled-cluster theory expands the wavefunction as exp(T) acting on a reference determinant, with cluster operator T = T_1 + T_2 + ... generating singly, doubly, and higher excitations. CCSD(T), which adds perturbative triples to coupled-cluster singles and doubles, achieves chemical accuracy of about 4 kilojoules per mole on reaction energies for first-row systems and serves as the gold standard against which density functional approximations are benchmarked.

The Born-Haber cycle for ionic compounds decomposes the formation enthalpy into atomisation, ionisation energy, electron affinity, sublimation, and lattice energy contributions. For NaCl the cycle gives a lattice enthalpy that matches the Madelung electrostatic calculation within a few percent, confirming the predominantly ionic character of the bonding.

Synthesis of transactinide elements proceeds through fusion of accelerated heavy ion beams with actinide targets. Element 117, tennessine, was first produced by bombarding berkelium-249 with calcium-48 ions, generating six atoms of tennessine-294 over months of beam time. Each atom survives only seconds before alpha decay; chemical separations performed atom-at-a-time on the heaviest synthesisable nuclides probe whether relativistic effects disrupt the expected periodic trends.

Sulphur catenates more readily than oxygen, forming chains and rings because the sulphur-sulphur single bond is comparatively strong. The thermodynamically stable form at room temperature is the crown-shaped S8 ring, which on melting and further heating opens into long polymeric chains, sharply increasing the viscosity of the liquid before it falls again near the boiling point.

The Joule-Thomson effect describes the temperature change of a real gas forced through a throttle at constant enthalpy. Below its inversion temperature a gas cools on expansion because work is done against attractive forces, the basis of gas liquefaction. Hydrogen and helium have inversion temperatures below room temperature, so they warm on throttling unless precooled first.

Photolysis of carboxylic acids decorated with photolabile protecting groups such as ortho-nitrobenzyl esters releases the free acid upon irradiation at 365 nanometres. The ortho-nitro group abstracts a benzylic hydrogen in the excited state to give an aci-nitro intermediate that fragments to release a nitrosobenzaldehyde and the carboxylate. Caged compounds based on this chemistry deliver biological effectors with spatiotemporal control in living cells.

In a redox titration the potential of the solution is governed by the couple in excess, jumping sharply at the equivalence point as control passes from the analyte couple to the titrant couple. The equivalence-point potential is a weighted average of the two standard potentials, the weights set by the number of electrons each half-reaction transfers.

The noble gases were long thought wholly unreactive until xenon was found to combine with the most powerful oxidants. Xenon difluoride, tetrafluoride, and hexafluoride form by direct reaction with fluorine, the heavier noble gas being oxidisable because its outermost electrons are weakly held. Xenon trioxide is a dangerously explosive solid that hydrolyses from the hexafluoride.

The inductive effect explains why trichloroacetic acid, with pKa 0.66, is far stronger than acetic acid at pKa 4.76. Three electronegative chlorine atoms withdraw electron density through the sigma framework, stabilising the carboxylate anion and shifting the dissociation equilibrium toward the ionised form. Each successive chlorine substitution lowers the pKa by roughly one to two units.

Surface tension arises because molecules at a liquid surface experience a net inward attraction, having fewer neighbours than those in the bulk. Water has a high surface tension of about 72 millinewtons per metre at room temperature, a direct consequence of its hydrogen-bonding network, which allows small insects to stand on a pond and droplets to bead on a waxy leaf.

The citric acid cycle oxidises acetyl-CoA in eight enzymatic steps within the mitochondrial matrix, generating three NADH, one FADH2, and one GTP per turn, along with two CO2 molecules. Citrate synthase initiates the cycle by condensing oxaloacetate and acetyl-CoA; isocitrate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase provide the major regulatory points.

Machine-learning interatomic potentials such as Behler-Parrinello neural networks and Gaussian approximation potentials learn the potential energy surface from a curated training set of high-level electronic structure calculations. Linear scaling with system size and orders-of-magnitude speedup over ab initio dynamics permit microsecond trajectories of thousands of atoms. Active learning protocols add new configurations encountered during simulation, iteratively improving the potential where it is queried farthest from training data.

subtopic: peptide bond formation and protecting groups
sentence: A peptide bond forms by condensation of the carboxyl group of one amino acid with the amino group of another, expelling water. The reaction is thermodynamically unfavourable in aqueous solution, so synthesis activates the carboxyl as a reactive ester or anhydride first, and the resulting amide adopts a planar trans geometry stabilised by partial double-bond character.

Atomic layer deposition grows conformal thin films one atomic layer at a time through alternating self-limiting surface reactions. Trimethylaluminium and water alternately exposed to a silicon wafer produce Al2O3 at a growth rate near 0.1 nanometres per cycle. The conformality permits coating of high-aspect-ratio features down to nanometre dimensions, central to gate dielectric deposition in modern transistor manufacturing.

The diagonal relationship pairs an element with the one to its lower right, which often shares similar charge density. Lithium resembles magnesium more than the other alkali metals: both form covalent organometallics, burn in nitrogen to give nitrides, and have sparingly soluble carbonates and fluorides, a similarity traced to comparable ionic radius to charge ratios.

The Nernst equation corrects a standard potential for non-standard concentrations, the potential decreasing by 59 millivolts per decade increase in the ratio of oxidised to reduced species for a one-electron couple. For the ferric-ferrous couple this means the measured potential reports directly on the activity ratio, allowing redox titrations to be followed potentiometrically to a precise endpoint.

Hydrogen fluoride forms zigzag hydrogen-bonded chains in the liquid and retains polymeric association even in the vapour, where the average aggregate approaches a hexamer near the boiling point. The strong hydrogen bonding and high polarity of the H-F bond make anhydrous hydrogen fluoride a weakly conducting, strongly self-ionising solvent quite unlike the other hydrogen halides.

The method of initial rates determines reaction orders by comparing rates measured at the very start of the reaction for systematically varied starting concentrations. Doubling [A] while holding [B] fixed and observing the rate quadruple establishes second order in A. Combining several such experiments isolates each exponent and finally yields the rate constant from the complete rate expression.

Gas chromatography separates volatile analytes by partition between a mobile carrier gas and a stationary phase coating the capillary column. Retention times depend on volatility and chemical affinity for the stationary phase. Coupled to a mass spectrometer detector through a heated transfer line, GC-MS provides both quantitative and structural information in a single analysis.

The radical chlorination of methane shows poor selectivity because the chlorine atom is highly reactive and abstracts hydrogen with a low activation barrier, so even slightly stronger bonds are attacked at competitive rates. Bromination is far more selective because the bromine atom is less reactive, giving a later transition state that discriminates sharply among C-H bond strengths.

Alpha decay proceeds through quantum tunnelling of the alpha particle through the Coulomb barrier of the parent nucleus. The Geiger-Nuttall law relates the decay constant to the alpha particle energy through log lambda = a - b/sqrt(E), accounting for variations in half-lives over twenty orders of magnitude across the actinides. Polonium-212 decays in 0.3 microseconds while uranium-238 lives 4.5 billion years.

A back-titration suits a slow or insoluble analyte. To assay calcium carbonate the sample is dissolved in a measured excess of standard hydrochloric acid, and after reaction is complete the unconsumed acid is titrated with standard sodium hydroxide. Subtracting the base used from the acid originally added gives the acid that the carbonate consumed.

Cross-linked polyacrylamide gels formed from acrylamide and N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide with ammonium persulphate initiator and TEMED accelerator provide the matrix for SDS-PAGE separations. The mesh size depends on total monomer concentration T and cross-linker fraction C; 12 percent T with 2.7 percent C resolves proteins between 15 and 60 kilodaltons. The Ferguson plot of log mobility versus T yields free-solution mobility and retardation coefficient.

The aromatic transition state model rationalises pericyclic selectivity by counting electrons in the cyclic array of interacting orbitals. A transition state with 4n plus 2 electrons and zero phase inversions is Huckel aromatic and thermally allowed, while one with the same electron count and an odd number of inversions is Mobius and requires photochemical activation, reproducing the Woodward-Hoffmann conclusions.

The first law of thermodynamics states that the change in internal energy of a closed system equals the heat added minus the work done by the system, Delta U = Q - W. For an ideal gas undergoing isothermal expansion, the work done is W = nRT ln(V2/V1), and since the internal energy depends only on temperature, Q must equal W exactly.

A carbocation rearranges when a hydrogen or alkyl group migrates from an adjacent carbon to convert a less stable cation into a more stable one. A secondary carbocation flanked by a quaternary carbon undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to become a tertiary cation, and the migrating group moves with its bonding electron pair so that no separate intermediate forms.

The Claisen rearrangement of an allyl vinyl ether is a [3,3]-sigmatropic process that converts the ether into a gamma,delta-unsaturated carbonyl compound. The reaction is exothermic because a weaker carbon-oxygen pi bond is traded for a stronger carbon-oxygen sigma bond, and it proceeds through an ordered chair-like transition state that transfers chirality with high fidelity.

Lanthanide contraction refers to the steady decrease in ionic radius across the 4f series, due to incomplete shielding of the increasing nuclear charge by f electrons. The contraction makes the radii of the post-lanthanide third-row transition metals nearly identical to their second-row congeners; hafnium and zirconium have almost the same ionic radius, complicating their chemical separation.

Deoxofluorination reagents such as diethylaminosulfur trifluoride convert a hydroxyl group into a fluoride with inversion of configuration at carbon. The reagent first activates the oxygen as a leaving group, and fluoride then displaces it through a backside attack, providing a direct route to secondary alkyl fluorides from readily available alcohols.

The chemical oxygen demand of a water sample is measured by refluxing it with excess dichromate in strong sulphuric acid with a silver catalyst. Organic matter is oxidised, consuming dichromate in proportion to its concentration, and the unreacted dichromate is back-titrated with ferrous ammonium sulphate, the difference revealing how much oxidant the pollutants consumed.

Bulk metallic glasses such as Zr41.2Ti13.8Cu12.5Ni10Be22.5 form amorphous solids upon casting because the multi-component composition frustrates crystallisation. The deep eutectic suppresses the melting point, broadening the supercooled liquid region above the glass transition. The resulting alloy has yield strength near 1.9 gigapascals and elastic strain limit close to 2 percent, twice that of conventional crystalline steels.

Photoinduced electron-transfer catalysis with organic photocatalysts such as acridinium salts and Eosin Y replaces precious-metal complexes for visible-light driven transformations. The lifetimes of their excited states fall in the nanosecond range with redox potentials sufficient to oxidise electron-rich alkenes or reduce aryl halides. Catalyst loadings of 1 mole percent and ambient temperature operation lower the environmental footprint of radical-based syntheses.

Mercury cycling between atmosphere, ocean, and soil is dominated by the long lifetime of elemental Hg(0) in the gas phase, several months to a year, allowing global redistribution from emission sources. Oxidation to Hg(II) by bromine atoms in polar sunrise produces atmospheric mercury depletion events; deposited Hg(II) is methylated in sediments and bioaccumulates as methylmercury through the aquatic food web, biomagnifying by factors approaching 10^6 in top predators.

Osazone formation occurs when a reducing sugar reacts with three equivalents of phenylhydrazine, derivatising both C1 and C2 as phenylhydrazones. Because C2 is consumed, glucose, mannose, and fructose all yield the identical osazone, a classic observation that established their stereochemical relationship at C3, C4, and C5 long before modern spectroscopy.

Chain elongation in terpene biosynthesis proceeds by ionisation of the pyrophosphate leaving group to form an allylic carbocation, which is attacked by the terminal double bond of isopentenyl pyrophosphate. Loss of a proton regenerates a double bond, and repeated cycles extend the chain to geranyl, farnesyl, and geranylgeranyl pyrophosphates of progressively greater length.

Werner's coordination theory distinguishes primary and secondary valence in metal complexes. The primary valence corresponds to the oxidation state and is balanced by counterions, while the secondary valence corresponds to the coordination number and identifies the directly bonded ligands. The geometric isomerism of [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+, with violet cis and green trans forms, provided early experimental confirmation.

The ideal gas law PV equals nRT combines the empirical relations of Boyle, Charles, and Avogadro into a single equation of state. For one mole of gas at 273.15 kelvin and one atmosphere the molar volume works out to 22.4 litres, a benchmark that follows directly from substituting the gas constant 8.314 joules per mole kelvin and converting units consistently.

The integration of a proton NMR signal is proportional to the number of equivalent protons giving rise to it. In ethyl acetate the spectrum shows a triplet near 1.2 ppm integrating for three, a singlet near 2.0 ppm integrating for three, and a quartet near 4.1 ppm integrating for two, the relative areas immediately revealing the ethyl and acetyl fragments.

Crown ethers are macrocyclic polyethers that bind alkali metal cations through ion-dipole interactions with the ring oxygen atoms. 18-crown-6 has an optimal cavity diameter of 0.26 to 0.32 nanometres for potassium ion, with binding constants in methanol exceeding 10^6 inverse molar. The size-match selectivity transports K+ across nonpolar membranes that would otherwise reject the hydrated cation, enabling phase-transfer catalysis with potassium hydroxide.

Replacing a hydrogen with fluorine in a drug candidate often blocks oxidative metabolism at that position because the carbon-fluorine bond resists cleavage by cytochrome enzymes. The small steric demand of fluorine, comparable to hydrogen, lets the substitution proceed without major conformational disruption while modulating the molecule's lipophilicity and acidity.

Arsenic contamination of groundwater in Bangladesh originates from reductive dissolution of arsenic-bearing iron oxyhydroxides under anoxic alluvial aquifer conditions. Concentrations exceeding the WHO guideline of 10 micrograms per litre affect tens of millions of people drinking from shallow tube wells. Co-precipitation with iron is the practical treatment: aeration oxidises As(III) to As(V), and Fe(III) flocs adsorb the arsenate, removing it from the water column.

The pentose phosphate pathway parallels glycolysis and provides NADPH for reductive biosynthesis and ribose-5-phosphate for nucleotide synthesis. The oxidative branch is irreversible and committed by glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase; the non-oxidative branch is reversible and interconverts five-, four-, six-, and seven-carbon sugars through transketolase and transaldolase reactions.

Pyranose rings adopt chair conformations, and beta-D-glucopyranose is exceptionally stable because every bulky substituent, including all four hydroxyls and the hydroxymethyl group, can occupy an equatorial position simultaneously. This all-equatorial arrangement minimises 1,3-diaxial strain and accounts for glucose being the most abundant monosaccharide in nature.

A redox indicator changes colour over a narrow potential range bracketing its own standard potential, by analogy with the way a pH indicator responds to a span of pH. Ferroin, the iron complex of phenanthroline, switches from pale blue to red near 1.06 volts and is the indicator of choice for titrations with cerium and dichromate.

The non-mevalonate, or methylerythritol phosphate, pathway operates in plant plastids and many bacteria, building isopentenyl pyrophosphate from pyruvate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate rather than from acetyl-CoA. Its absence in humans makes the enzymes of this route attractive targets for antimalarial and antibacterial drug design.

Cholesterol biosynthesis proceeds from acetyl-CoA through HMG-CoA, mevalonate, and isoprenoid intermediates, with HMG-CoA reductase the rate-limiting and pharmacologically pivotal step. Statins competitively inhibit this enzyme, lowering serum LDL cholesterol by upregulating hepatic LDL receptors in response to depleted intracellular cholesterol pools.

An ester is cleaved to a carboxylate salt and an alcohol by aqueous base in the reaction known as saponification. The mechanism proceeds through a tetrahedral intermediate formed by hydroxide addition to the carbonyl, and because the carboxylate product is stabilised and unreactive toward the alcohol, the reaction is irreversible, unlike acid-catalysed ester hydrolysis.

Bioisosteric replacement substitutes a group with another of similar steric and electronic properties while preserving biological activity. Replacing a phenyl with thiophene, a carboxylic acid with tetrazole, or a methylene with sulphonyl can improve metabolic stability without sacrificing affinity. The classical and non-classical bioisosteres compiled by Patani and LaVoie continue to guide rational design of new chemical matter from established starting points.

Cyclic voltammetry sweeps the working electrode potential linearly between two limits and measures the resulting current. Reversible electron transfer at a planar electrode gives a peak-shaped i-E curve with anodic-cathodic peak separation of 59 mV/n at room temperature. The Randles-Sevcik equation relates peak current to the square root of scan rate for diffusion-controlled processes.

Radical halogenation of alkanes proceeds by a chain mechanism: initiation by homolysis of X2 under heat or light gives halogen atoms, propagation involves hydrogen abstraction from the substrate followed by halogen atom abstraction from a second X2 molecule. Bromination is highly selective for tertiary C-H bonds, while chlorination is faster but less selective due to a more reactive Cl radical.

Perovskite solar absorbers based on methylammonium lead iodide CH3NH3PbI3 exhibit band gaps near 1.55 electron volts, high absorption coefficients exceeding 10^4 inverse centimetres in the visible, and long electron-hole diffusion lengths of microns in polycrystalline films. Cell efficiencies have risen from 4 percent in 2009 to above 25 percent in single-junction architectures, with stability against moisture and ion migration remaining the principal commercialisation challenge.

Ferrocene Fe(C5H5)2 has eclipsed and staggered conformations within 4 kilojoules per mole of each other, sandwiched between two cyclopentadienyl rings. The iron centre is formally Fe(II) with the cyclopentadienide rings each donating six electrons in eta-5 coordination. Substitution chemistry on the rings parallels electrophilic aromatic substitution but proceeds far more readily, giving acetylferrocene from acetylation conditions that would fail on benzene.

Biomass valorisation routes convert lignocellulose into platform chemicals. Acid hydrolysis of cellulose yields glucose, which dehydrates to 5-hydroxymethylfurfural and further to levulinic acid and gamma-valerolactone. Hydrodeoxygenation over Pt/C catalysts upgrades these oxygenates to liquid fuels, while controlled oxidations yield furandicarboxylic acid as a biobased monomer for polyethylene furanoate, a renewable replacement for polyethylene terephthalate.

Polar protic solvents stabilise the transition state of an SN1 reaction by solvating the developing carbocation and the departing anion through hydrogen bonding and dipole interactions. The same solvents retard SN2 reactions because they cage the nucleophile in a hydrogen-bonded shell that must be partly stripped away before the nucleophile can attack.

Mass spectrometry ionises analytes and separates the resulting ions by mass-to-charge ratio. Electron impact ionisation gives fragmentation patterns that fingerprint molecular structure, while electrospray ionisation produces multiply charged ions of intact proteins. High resolution mass spectrometers measure m/z to several decimal places, allowing molecular formulae to be inferred from accurate masses.

Isotopes of an element share the same number of protons but differ in neutrons, so they are chemically nearly identical yet differ in mass and nuclear stability. Chlorine occurs as a mixture of chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 in roughly a three-to-one ratio, which is why its atomic weight on the periodic table is the non-integer value 35.45.

The Arrhenius equation k = A exp(-E_a/RT) expresses the temperature dependence of rate constants in terms of an activation energy E_a and pre-exponential factor A. Plotting ln k against 1/T gives a straight line with slope -E_a/R and intercept ln A. Transition state theory provides a more detailed treatment with k = (k_B T/h) exp(-Delta G_double_dagger /RT).

The cheletropic extrusion of sulphur dioxide from a cyclic sulphone expels the small molecule in a single concerted step, leaving behind a diene. The reverse addition of sulphur dioxide to a diene is likewise concerted, and the linear or non-linear approach of the extruding fragment is dictated by orbital symmetry, in parallel with the rules governing electrocyclic reactions.

Nuclear fission of uranium-235 by thermal neutrons proceeds through a compound nucleus that splits asymmetrically into two daughter nuclei with mass numbers around 95 and 137, releasing 200 megaelectron volts of energy per event together with two to three prompt neutrons. The resulting neutrons sustain a chain reaction if multiplication factor k exceeds unity, the operating principle of fission reactors moderated to thermal energies.

Hydrogen bonding occurs when a hydrogen atom bonded to a small electronegative atom is attracted to a lone pair on another such atom. The anomalously high boiling point of water, far above that of hydrogen sulphide, arises because each water molecule forms up to four hydrogen bonds, a three-dimensional network that must be partly broken before the liquid can vaporise.

The kinetic theory of gases derives pressure from molecular collisions with the container walls, yielding the result that pressure times volume equals one third of N m times the mean square speed. Equating this to nRT shows that the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule is three halves kT, depending only on temperature and not on the identity of the gas.

Hydrogen bonded quadruplexes of 2-ureido-4-pyrimidone units dimerise with association constants near 10^8 inverse molar in chloroform through four cooperative hydrogen bonds in a DDAA-AADD arrangement. Incorporation into telechelic polymer chains gives supramolecular polymers whose chain length increases reversibly with concentration. The viscosity of such systems rises sharply above a critical concentration where end-to-end coupling produces effectively high molecular weight species.

Conformational analysis of cyclohexane shows the chair as the lowest-energy form, with substituents preferring equatorial positions to avoid 1,3-diaxial strain. The A value quantifies this preference; tert-butyl has an A value near 21 kilojoules per mole, so it locks the ring with the bulky group equatorial. Ring flipping interconverts axial and equatorial positions through the higher-energy twist-boat.

Hydrazine, formally a hydride of nitrogen with an N-N single bond, is a powerful reducing agent and rocket propellant. Its decomposition to nitrogen, ammonia, and hydrogen is strongly exothermic, and catalytic decomposition over iridium furnishes a monopropellant thruster gas. The molecule adopts a gauche conformation that minimises lone-pair repulsion across the central bond.

The high electronegativity of fluorine makes a fluorinated alkyl chain both hydrophobic and lipophobic, so perfluorinated surfactants segregate to interfaces more strongly than hydrocarbon analogues. This dual phobicity drives fluorous-phase separation, in which a heavily fluorinated molecule partitions selectively into a perfluorocarbon solvent immiscible with both water and ordinary organic solvents.

The reactivity of carboxylic acid derivatives toward nucleophilic acyl substitution follows the order acyl chloride greater than anhydride greater than ester greater than amide. The order tracks the leaving-group ability and the degree to which the heteroatom donates electron density into the carbonyl, since better donation deactivates the carbon and a better leaving group accelerates collapse of the tetrahedral intermediate.

Solid sodium chloride adopts a face-centred cubic structure with chloride ions at the corners and face centres of a cube and sodium ions in the octahedral holes. Each ion has six counterion neighbours and the lattice energy of about 787 kJ/mol explains the high melting point and aqueous solubility, with hydration enthalpies just compensating the lattice energy on dissolution.

Sharpless dihydroxylation of alkenes uses OsO4 plus a chiral cinchona alkaloid ligand to deliver vicinal diols with high enantiomeric excess. The (DHQD)2PHAL ligand directs dihydroxylation to the alpha face, while (DHQ)2PHAL delivers the beta face product. Regeneration of OsO4 by N-methylmorpholine N-oxide allows catalytic loading. The transformation was a key piece of the 2001 Nobel Prize for chiral catalysis.

Ocean acidification reduces seawater pH by approximately 0.1 unit since pre-industrial times as anthropogenic CO2 dissolves and shifts the carbonate equilibrium toward bicarbonate and protons. The calcium carbonate saturation state Omega decreases as carbonate ion concentration falls, threatening calcifying organisms once Omega drops below unity. Polar oceans, with naturally lower carbonate concentrations from cold-water solubility, will become undersaturated for aragonite first.

Allosteric regulation of phosphofructokinase-1 by ATP and AMP couples glycolytic flux to cellular energy charge. High ATP allosterically inhibits the enzyme, while AMP relieves this inhibition. Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate, produced by a bifunctional kinase/phosphatase responsive to glucagon and insulin signalling, is a potent allosteric activator that integrates hormonal control with substrate availability.

Methane has a global warming potential of 28 over 100 years and 84 over 20 years, reflecting its much shorter atmospheric lifetime relative to carbon dioxide. Its tropospheric oxidation chain proceeds through CH3, CH3O2, CH3OOH or CH2O, CHO, and CO, with each step generating ozone in the presence of NOx and consuming an OH radical along the way.

subtopic: peptide bond formation and protecting groups
sentence: Aspartimide formation is a notorious side reaction in which the side-chain carbonyl of an aspartate residue is attacked by the backbone amide nitrogen of the following residue, forming a cyclic imide. The imide can then open to either the desired alpha-peptide or an unwanted beta-peptide, and bulky aspartate protecting groups are chosen specifically to suppress the cyclisation.

Allylic bromination with N-bromosuccinimide proceeds by a radical chain in which the succinimide reagent maintains a low, steady concentration of molecular bromine. The low bromine concentration favours hydrogen abstraction at the weak allylic C-H bond over addition across the double bond, so substitution rather than addition becomes the dominant pathway.

Mechanochemistry performs reactions in ball mills without solvent, exploiting mechanical energy transferred at the impact of grinding balls. Cocrystal formation, Suzuki couplings, and metal-organic framework synthesis all proceed efficiently under these conditions. The kinetic energy delivered to a small reaction volume generates local hot spots and creates fresh surface area on solid reactants, often enabling transformations that fail in solution because of poor reactant solubility.
